Anchoring PR-title/description feedback here, since this PR adds no `changelog.d/` fragment and these two rows are the visible surface of the part the description never mentions.

**The description no longer matches the code.** It walks through `handler.start_inference(...)` / `inv.stop()`, but head uses `handler.inference()` as a context manager. It sets out `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN` and devotes a whole "Private `_initialize()` call" section to justifying a private API call — neither exists at head, which sets only `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT` and `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_EMIT_EVENT`. That section explicitly invites reviewer input ("Happy to explore alternatives"), and the PR is already approved, so there's a real chance it was approved against a concern that no longer applies. Worth rewriting before merge so the record reflects what's actually being merged.

**"in line with the handler-based pattern used by the other reference libraries"** is not accurate — `git grep -l opentelemetry-util-genai` at the merge base returns nothing. This is the first scenario to take that dependency, which makes it a precedent for the other 28 rather than a catch-up. That's worth stating plainly, since it's the more interesting claim.

**"All four scenarios are migrated"** — the table lists three, and `scenario.py` defines three.

**Neither the title nor the description mentions the metric-coverage expansion**, which is these two rows. Adding `gen_ai.client.token.usage` and `gen_ai.client.operation.duration` to `METRIC_SPECS` reverses a documented maintainer decision and is the largest change in the PR by blast radius: two new report files, this README table, `data.json` churn in agent-framework and google-adk, and a rewrite of metric parsing/classification. Under a title scoped to "migrate anthropic reference scenario", that is easy to approve without noticing. See my comment on `semconv_model.py` — my preference is to split it out; if it stays, the title and description need to cover it.

Two problems here.

**1. The emitted value is hardcoded rather than derived.** `"Continue this long conversation."` now appears twice in this file — once in `messages` and once in this literal — so the telemetry can silently drift from the request that was actually sent. The pre-migration code derived this from `messages` via `input_messages(messages)`. `.github/instructions/reference-scenarios.instructions.md`: *"For attributes whose value is not truly static for the scenario, do not hardcode the emitted value... If the same non-static value is needed in both the SDK call and span attributes, bind it once locally and reuse it."* Note `_has_compaction_block_in_input(messages)` on line 163 still reads the real messages, so half the emission is derived and half is a literal.

**2. Setting this through `inv.attributes` corrupts the event, not just the span.** In util-genai 1.0b0, `InferenceInvocation._maybe_create_event()` builds event attributes with `get_content_attributes(for_span=False)` — a structured `list[dict]` — and then does `attributes.update(self.attributes)` **last**. So `inv.attributes` overrides the event too, and `gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details` ends up with `gen_ai.input.messages` as a JSON **string** here while `run_chat` and `run_chat_with_document_input` emit it as a structured list. Same library, same event, two different value shapes. `data.json` only records attribute *names*, so CI cannot catch this.

Both are fixable without any new type: `dataclasses.asdict` recurses into plain dicts, so a dict part inside `InputMessage` serializes to exactly the semconv compaction shape on both signals (verified: `asdict(InputMessage(role="assistant", parts=[{"type": "compaction"}]))` -> `{"role": "assistant", "parts": [{"type": "compaction"}]}`).

```suggestion
        # Compaction blocks have no util-genai part type, but `dataclasses.asdict`
        # recurses into plain dicts, so a dict part reaches the span and the event
        # in the same semconv shape.
        compaction_message, user_message = messages
        inv.input_messages = [  # -> gen_ai.input.messages
            InputMessage(role=compaction_message["role"], parts=[{"type": "compaction"}]),
            InputMessage(role=user_message["role"], parts=[Text(content=user_message["content"])]),
        ]
```

Heads-up: with this and the `gen_ai.output.messages` suggestion (line 185) applied, `import json` on line 9 becomes unused and ruff F401 will fail — drop it in the same change.

I checked this against the pinned Weaver (`v0.24.2`) instead of assuming, and **all three non-list branches here are unreachable**. `SampleMetric` is declared as:

```rust
pub struct SampleMetric {
    pub name: String,
    pub instrument: SampleInstrument,
    pub unit: String,
    pub data_points: Option<DataPoints>,   // <- no skip_serializing_if
    pub live_check_result: Option<LiveCheckResult>,
}

#[serde(untagged)]
pub enum DataPoints {
    Number(Vec<SampleNumberDataPoint>),
    Histogram(Vec<SampleHistogramDataPoint>),
    ExponentialHistogram(Vec<SampleExponentialHistogramDataPoint>),
}
```

- `data_points` has no `#[serde(skip_serializing_if)]`, so the key is **always present** (`null` when empty). `raw_points is marker` never happens, so `return [metric]` is dead.
- `DataPoints` is an untagged enum over `Vec`s, so it always serializes as an **array**. The `isinstance(raw_points, dict)` branch is dead.
- `SampleMetric` has **no `data` field at all**, so the `metric["data"]["data_points"]` lookup is dead, and the docstring's "either known Weaver metric shapes" doesn't describe anything Weaver emits.

Confirmed empirically as well: I ran `uv run run-scenario google-adk` against Weaver v0.24.2 and every one of the 16 metric samples in `live_check.json` had keys exactly `['data_points', 'instrument', 'live_check_result', 'name', 'unit']`, with `data_points` a list. No `data` key, no dict, no absent key.

**The shape that is real is the one this function mishandles.** `otlp_data_to_data_points` in `src/registry/otlp/conversion.rs` ends in `_ => None`, so a Summary metric (or one with no data set) serializes as `"data_points": null`. That falls past all three checks into the final warning and is reported as `invalid data_points ... got NoneType` — a valid Weaver serialization logged as invalid. `_summarize_samples` already treats an empty result as "nothing to record" (`if observations is None or not observations: continue`), so `None` should simply map to `[]`.

```suggestion
def _metric_data_points(metric: dict[str, object]) -> list[dict[str, object]] | None:
    """Return the metric's data points, or None if `data_points` is unusable."""
    raw_points = metric.get("data_points")
    if raw_points is None:
        return []
    if not isinstance(raw_points, list):
        _LOGGER.warning(
            "Skipping metric %r with invalid data_points: expected list, got %s",
            metric.get("name", ""),
            type(raw_points).__name__,
        )
        return None

    data_points: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for data_point in raw_points:
        if isinstance(data_point, dict):
            data_points.append(data_point)
            continue
        _LOGGER.warning(
            "Skipping non-dict data point for metric %r: %r",
            metric.get("name", ""),
            data_point,
        )
    return data_points
```

I applied this on top of this branch and checked it: `ruff check src`, `ruff format --check src`, and the existing `tests/` suite all pass.

These don't need to be set before the imports. `get_content_capturing_mode()` and `should_emit_event()` both read `os.environ` on every call, and the only value cached at construction time is `TelemetryHandler._capture_content` — built in `TelemetryHandler.__init__`, which this scenario only reaches via `get_telemetry_handler()` inside `main()`. Setting them at the top of `main()` is enough, and it lets the imports be a normal single block.

This turns one Anthropic response into N assistant messages, one per content block. `response_output_messages()` (the helper this replaces) built a single assistant message holding all the parts, and that's what the convention requires — `gen-ai-spans.md` on `gen_ai.output.messages`: "Each message corresponds to exactly one generation (choice/candidate) and vice versa - one choice cannot be split across multiple messages."

The mock only ever returns one text block, so `data.json` and the reports don't move either way; the shape is just wrong for any real multi-block response (text + thinking, text + compaction).

The guard matters too: with the current comprehension a response with no text blocks yields `[]` and no attribute, so keep that behaviour rather than emitting a message with empty `parts`. This also lines up with how `run_compaction` builds its output below.

```suggestion
        output_parts = [Text(content=block.text) for block in resp.content if hasattr(block, "text")]
        if output_parts:
            inv.output_messages = [  # -> gen_ai.output.messages
                OutputMessage(role="assistant", parts=output_parts, finish_reason=resp.stop_reason)
            ]
```

- **`run_chat_with_document_input` now emits an event.** It only produced a span before this PR.
